newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EA-Generali eyes CA local banks.
newsitem.headline: EA-Generali eyes CA local banks.

text.p: Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali said it was eyeing a stake in Creditanstalt Bankverein's regional banking interests following a failed bid earlier this year for a stake in Creditanstalt itself.

Bank Austria, which won the race for the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares, has said it is prepared to part with stakes in three regional banks -- Bank fuer Kaernten und Steiermark (BKS), Bank fuer Oberoesterreich und Salzburg (Oberbank) and Bank fuer Tirol und Vorarlberg (BTV).

"The three banks have captured our interest," EA-Generali chief executive Dietrich Karner told reporters, adding that EA-Generali was unwilling to take over all of Creditanstalt's shares in the three.
Negotiations cannot go ahead, however, until the European Commission has approved the Creditanstalt sale. A decision is not expected before mid-March.

EA-Generali, which owns 4.48 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares, said it may also take on Creditanstalt's 49 percent stake in insurance joint venture CA-Generali. EA-Generali has a 51 percent share in the business.
"We have an option to buy," Karner said.

EA-Generali, which was part of an international consortium bidding for Creditanstalt, said it was disappointed at the Austrian government's decision to sell to Bank Austria. Scope for greater synergy effects and increased cooperation had been lost, Karner explained.
"But it isn't a matter of survival for us. It does not pose us any difficulties," he added.
CA-Generali contributed around 1.2 billion schillings to EA-Generali group life insurance premium volume of 10.5 billion, Karner said.
EA-Generali's total premium volume rose to 42 billion schillings last year from 36.88 billion in 1995. The firm will release preliminary 1996 results on March 6. --- Vienna newsroom, +43 1 531 12 254
